Looking at the pull request, I need to identify real problems worth flagging. Let me analyze each file carefully:

1. **`CalendarService.ts` line 1024**: `updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` passes an empty data object. The comment on lines 1022-1023 says "Update SelectedCalendar.updatedAt for all calendars under this credential" but Prisma's `updateMany` either throws an error or is a no-op with empty data. Either way, the intent isn't satisfied.

2. **`scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` line 68**: Uses `sed -i '' -E` which is macOS-specific syntax that fails on Linux.

3. **`CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx`**: Hardcodes "en-US" locale for date formatting regardless of the user's actual locale.

4. **Missing tests**: The entire new feature (mutation, repository method, React component) has no test coverage.

5. **Cache status query doesn't filter by `expiresAt`**: The new `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` returns cache status even for expired entries, while cache reads filter by expiry.

findings.title: updateManyByCredentialId called with empty data
findings.body: The new call `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` passes an empty `data` object. Prisma's `updateMany` either rejects empty data with a validation error (which would break the unwatchCalendar flow that invokes this) or silently performs no update. In neither case does it update `updatedAt` as the preceding comment claims, so `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` is never set by this code path. The intended behavior must be achieved by passing an explicit field, e.g. `{ updatedAt: new Date() }`.

findings.title: Comment misrepresents code behavior
findings.body: The comment `// Update SelectedCalendar.updatedAt for all calendars under this credential` directly precedes a `updateManyByCredentialId` call with empty `data`. The call does not update `updatedAt`, so the comment is inaccurate and misleading to anyone reading the code.

findings.title: macOS-only sed syntax breaks script on Linux
findings.body: Line 68 uses `sed -i '' -E "..."` which is BSD/macOS sed syntax. On Linux, `sed -i` requires either no argument or a suffix as an extension (e.g. `sed -i.bak -E`). As written, the script will fail with a usage error on any non-macOS developer machine or CI runner, silently leaving `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` stale and breaking local webhook testing.

findings.title: Cache timestamp hardcoded to en-US locale
findings.body: `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` is used to format `cacheUpdatedAt`, ignoring the user's locale even though `useLocale()` is already invoked in the same component. Non-English-speaking users will see US-formatted dates (e.g. `12/31/2025, 4:30 PM`) instead of their own regional convention. The date-time key in common.json (`cache_last_updated`) is also a non-interpolated template, so the format cannot be easily localized downstream.

findings.title: Cache status query ignores expiresAt
findings.body: `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` calls `prisma.calendarCache.groupBy({ where: { credentialId: { in: credentialIds } } })` without filtering by `expiresAt`, unlike `getCachedAvailability` which only returns non-expired rows. A credential with only stale (expired) cache entries will still show a `cacheUpdatedAt` in the UI, causing users to see a 'Last updated' timestamp for cache that is no longer being served — and they may delete it under the mistaken assumption it is currently in use.

findings.title: No tests for new deleteCache tRPC handler
findings.body: The new `deleteCache` mutation is a destructive operation against `CalendarCache` keyed by a user-owned credential, yet no unit or integration tests are added covering ownership validation (e.g. missing credential, credential owned by another user) or successful cache deletion. This is the kind of authorization-sensitive path that warrants explicit test coverage before merging.

findings.title: No tests for new getCacheStatusByCredentialIds repository method
findings.body: The newly added `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` method is the data foundation for the new UI cache-status feature, but no tests were added (including the mock implementation in `calendar-cache.repository.mock.ts`). A test verifying that the method correctly groups by credentialId and returns null for credentials with no cache rows is missing.

findings.title: No tests for new CredentialActionsDropdown component
findings.body: The newly introduced `CredentialActionsDropdown` component (which replaces `DisconnectIntegration` and is rendered in the installed-calendars list) has no unit or e2e tests. The conditional render guard (no dropdown if neither disconnect is permitted nor a Google Calendar cache exists), the cache-status display, the confirmation dialogs, and the tRPC mutation success/error paths all lack coverage.
